hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.

paper.title: Cholesterol dysregulation in APOE4 astrocytes promotes α-synuclein pathology in miBrains.

findings.finding_description: Lysosomal proteolytic capacity was measured with DQ-BSA, a self-quenched substrate that fluoresces on lysosomal cleavage, in isogenic APOE4/4 versus APOE3/3 iPSC-derived astrocytes from two donor pairs. APOE4/4 astrocytes had significantly lower DQ-BSA signal (Donor #1 p=0.0032; Donor #2 p<0.0001). This is an acidification-dependent surrogate for lysosomal pH, not a direct endosomal pH measurement. Reduced proteolysis is more consistent with less acidic, not more acidic, compartments, so it argues weakly against the hypothesis.
findings.quote: APOE4/4 astrocytes showed significantly reduced lysosomal DQ-BSA signal compared to isogenic control APOE3/3 astrocytes across two isogenic donor pairs (Donor #1: p= 0.0032; Donor #2: p < 0.0001, Figure 4d)
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes show reduced lysosomal DQ-BSA proteolysis versus APOE3/3, a weak surrogate that does not support increased acidification.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 iPSC-derived human astrocytes (2 donor pairs)

findings.finding_description: DQ-BSA fluorescence was normalized to co-internalized, proteolysis-resistant dextran to separate per-lysosome function from lysosome number. APOE4/4 astrocytes still showed significantly lower proteolytic activity than APOE3/3 (p=0.0098). This indicates impaired degradative (pH-dependent) function per organelle, which is a surrogate for lumenal pH and gives no evidence of hyperacidification.
findings.quote: Even after dextran normalization, APOE4/4 astrocytes retained significantly lower proteolytic activity (p = 0.0098; Figure S4e)
findings.summary: Per-lysosome proteolytic activity is reduced in APOE4/4 astrocytes after dextran normalization.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 iPSC-derived human astrocytes

findings.finding_description: BafilomycinA1, a V-ATPase inhibitor that blocks acidification, suppressed DQ-BSA cleavage in both APOE3/3 (p<0.0001) and APOE4/4 (p=0.0174) astrocytes. This shows the readout depends on acidification, which supports DQ-BSA as a pH-linked surrogate. Class 5: the perturbation is of acidification rather than APOE genotype, and no genotype comparison of pH is made, so no directness class fits.
findings.quote: As expected, bafilomycinA1 suppressed DQ-BSA cleavage in both APOE3/3 (p < 0.0001) and APOE4/4 astrocytes (p = 0.0174; Figure S4e)
findings.summary: Blocking acidification abolishes the DQ-BSA signal in both genotypes, linking the proteolysis readout to lysosomal pH.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 iPSC-derived human astrocytes

findings.finding_description: Immunoreactivity for the lysosomal membrane protein LAMP1 was significantly reduced in APOE4/4 versus APOE3/3 astrocytes in two donor pairs (Donor #1 p=0.0002; Donor #2 p=0.0001). This indicates altered endolysosomal compartment mass, but it is only a distant surrogate for endosomal pH.
findings.quote: immunoreactivity for the lysosomal membrane protein LAMP1 was also significantly reduced in APOE4/4 astrocytes compared to isogenic APOE3/3 astrocytes (Donor #1: p = 0.0002 and Donor #2: p = 0.0001, Figure S4d)
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes have reduced LAMP1, indicating endolysosomal alteration but not pH directly.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 iPSC-derived human astrocytes (2 donor pairs)

findings.finding_description: Astrocytes were loaded with α-Syn-HiLyte for 24 h, extracellular α-Syn was removed, and the intracellular signal was tracked for a further 24 h. Intracellular signal fell significantly in APOE3/3 astrocytes (p<0.0001) but not in APOE4/4 astrocytes (p=0.694). This is impaired endolysosomal degradation, a very indirect surrogate for compartment pH.
findings.quote: APOE3/3 astrocytes showed a significant reduction in intracellular α-Syn-HiLyte signal (p < 0.0001), whereas APOE4/4 astrocytes showed no significant decrease (p = 0.694; Figure 4c), indicating impaired degradation of α-Syn.
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes fail to degrade internalized α-Syn, consistent with endolysosomal dysfunction.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 iPSC-derived human astrocytes

findings.finding_description: DQ-BSA fluorescence was normalized to co-internalized, proteolysis-resistant dextran. After normalization, APOE4/4 astrocytes still had lower proteolytic activity than APOE3/3 (p=0.0098). This indicates a per-organelle functional deficit, which could involve acidification, but pH was not measured.
findings.quote: Even after dextran normalization, APOE4/4 astrocytes retained significantly lower proteolytic activity (p = 0.0098; Figure S4e), indicating functional impairment rather than solely reduced lysosome abundance.
findings.summary: Per-lysosome proteolysis is lower in APOE4/4 astrocytes, consistent with impaired lysosomal function, possibly including acidification.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic iPSC-derived human APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 astrocytes

findings.finding_description: After 4 h of α-Syn-HiLyte uptake, the fraction of α-Syn co-localizing with LysoTracker (an acidotropic probe) was lower in APOE4/4 than in APOE3/3 astrocytes. This reflects delivery of cargo to acidic compartments, not pH per se.
findings.quote: the percentage of α-Syn-HiLyte that co-localized with LysoTracker decreased in APOE4/4 astrocytes compared to APOE3/3 (p = 0.0395; Figure S5f)
findings.summary: Less α-Syn reaches LysoTracker-positive acidic compartments in APOE4/4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic iPSC-derived human APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 astrocytes

findings.finding_description: Cholesterol extraction with MβCD increased LysoTracker-positive signal in APOE4/4 astrocytes (p=0.044), with similar effects across donors (Fig. S5d, p<0.0001). This implies the cholesterol-loaded APOE4 state has reduced acidic-compartment signal, but no APOE3 comparison of LysoTracker is reported in this text. The perturbation is cholesterol, a surrogate for APOE4, and the readout is LysoTracker, a surrogate for pH.
findings.quote: Consistent with improved lysosomal capacity, MβCD increased LysoTracker-positive lysosomal signal in APOE4/4 astrocytes (p = 0.044; Figure 5d)
findings.summary: Lowering cholesterol raises LysoTracker signal in APOE4/4 astrocytes, suggesting cholesterol-linked loss of acidic compartments.
findings.experimental_system: iPSC-derived human APOE4/4 astrocytes treated with MβCD/2HβCD

findings.finding_description: Bafilomycin A1, a V-ATPase inhibitor that blocks acidification, suppressed DQ-BSA cleavage in both APOE3/3 (p<0.0001) and APOE4/4 (p=0.0174) astrocytes. This validates that the DQ-BSA surrogate depends on acidification. It is a control rather than an APOE4-vs-APOE3 pH comparison, so it is assigned class 5.
findings.quote: As expected, bafilomycinA1 suppressed DQ-BSA cleavage in both APOE3/3 (p < 0.0001) and APOE4/4 astrocytes (p = 0.0174; Figure S4e), confirming lysosome-dependent signal generation.
findings.summary: The DQ-BSA readout is acidification-dependent in both genotypes, supporting its use as a pH-linked surrogate.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic iPSC-derived human APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 astrocytes
